For most UK travellers visiting Europe, **Monzo is the simpler, lower-stress choice**, though **Revolut has stronger multi-currency features** if you don't mind managing your balances. 

---

### Key Comparison (Standard / Free Accounts)

| Feature | **Monzo** | **Revolut** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Exchange Rate** | Mastercard wholesale rate (excellent) | Interbank/Revolut market rate (marginally better midweek) |
| **Weekend Fees** | **None** (same rate 7 days a week) | **1% fee** on currency conversions from Friday evening to Sunday evening |
| **Monthly FX Cap** | **Unlimited** fee-free card spending | **£1,000/month** limit (1% fee afterwards) |
| **ATM Cash (in EEA)** | **£400 / rolling 30 days** fee-free (unlimited if Monzo is your main bank); 3% after | **£200 / rolling month** (or 5 withdrawals, whichever comes first); 2% after |
| **Hold Euros?** | No (converts automatically from GBP on spend) | **Yes** (hold EUR, exchange in advance, get local EUR IBAN) |
| **UK FSCS Protected?** | **Yes** (up to £85,000) | **No** (standard accounts rely on safeguarding rules) |

---

### Why Choose Monzo?

* **No weekend gotchas:** Financial markets close over the weekend. Monzo doesn't penalise you for this, whereas Revolut adds a 1% markup on weekend spending unless you've already converted your money to EUR beforehand.
* **True “tap and forget”:** There is no monthly cap on card spending abroad. If you book a nice hotel or spend heavily, you don't have to worry about hitting Revolut’s £1,000 monthly free exchange ceiling.
* **Better cash withdrawal terms:** If you need cash (which is still common in parts of Germany, Italy, or rural Europe), Monzo gives you double the allowance (£400 vs £200) in the European Economic Area (EEA).

---

### Why Choose Revolut?

* **Locking in exchange rates:** If the pound is performing well before your trip, you can convert money into a dedicated Euro pocket at midday on a Wednesday and hold it there. 
* **Widespread in Europe:** Revolut is much more common among mainland Europeans than Monzo. If you’re travelling with European friends, splitting bills or transferring money peer-to-peer is instant and painless.
* **Disposable virtual cards:** Great for booking train tickets, tours, or hotels on smaller European travel sites where you might be wary of card fraud.
* **In-app travel perks:** Revolut lets you purchase budget travel eSIMs directly in the app if you need data abroad.

---

### The Verdict

* **Pick Monzo** if you want zero hassle. You just spend like you would at home without watching calendars, converting balances, or worrying about weekend surcharges.
* **Pick Revolut** if you want to actively manage and hold Euros, or if you regularly spend/transfer money to European bank accounts.

**Top tip:** If you have both, **take both**. Keep Monzo as your primary card for everyday spending and weekend meals, and keep Revolut loaded as a backup card in case one gets lost, skimmed, or temporarily blocked. 

*(And remember: whichever card you use, **always choose to pay in EUR / local currency** at the card reader or ATM, never GBP, to avoid costly Dynamic Currency Conversion markups).*
